messages:
Kevin S: Heads-up: MapleBank (sales POC) sent an intake asking for Dedicated capacity sizing. Key asks: sustained throughput ~200 req/min, bursts up to 600 req/min for ~10m windows, avg response ~400 tokens, streaming enabled, session affinity + KV reuse, target P95 latency <= 1.2s. Can product/eng confirm ballpark pool and autoscale policy so I can respond with pricing and SLA tradeoffs? @Anna P
Anna P: Thanks Kevin. Quick clarifying Qs:
- model they intend to run? open 13B q4_0 or something bigger?
- are all sessions equivalent (same prompt size), any long-context usage?
- retention/idle timeout for cache?
Kevin S: They plan to use the 13B quantized variant (customer engineering confirms q4_0-ish), mostly homogeneous prompts, context ~2k tokens, KV cache wanted for session affinity, idle session timeout ~30m.
Sarah L: FWIW rough perf numbers from bench: 13B q4_0 on an A100-80 yields about 60 tokens/s sustained (varies with prompt/seq). For 400 tokens/output avg that's ~6.7s generation time per request if single-stream. With 200 req/min = 3.33 rps -> steady in-flight ~22 (3.33 * 6.7). For 600 req/min burst (10 rps) -> in-flight ~67.
Sarah L: In terms of GPUs, assuming ~8-12 concurrent in-flight requests per GPU with efficient batching and prefix cache, baseline pool ~= 2-3 GPUs to cover 22 in-flight (but that's optimistic). Real-world: recommend baseline 6 GPUs for headroom and queuing latency control. Autoscale up to 20-24 GPUs for burst windows to keep P95 <1.2s.
Devon R: Can we show the math quickly for sales?
Sarah L: Sure, simplified:
```
tokens_per_resp = 400
tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = 60
gen_time_per_req = tokens_per_resp / tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = ~6.7s
steady_rps = 200 / 60 = 3.33 rps
steady_inflight = steady_rps * gen_time_per_req = ~22
requests_per_gpu_concurrency = ~8-12 (depends on batching)
baseline_gpus = ceil(22 / 8) = 3 -> add ops buffer => 6
burst_rps = 600 / 60 = 10 rps
burst_inflight = 10 * 6.7 = ~67
burst_gpus = ceil(67 / 8) = 9 -> add headroom & rollback safety => 20-24 (to hit latency targets under worst-case strat)
```
Sarah L: Important caveats: streaming increases perceived latency constraints (we need headroom), KV cache reuse helps reduce work (but not token-generation cost), and real batching efficiency depends on request arrival distribution.
Oliver M: From Solutions: customer wants cost estimate and can accept a canary for launch (2-4 GPUs) + guaranteed burst capacity as SLA add-on. They prefer reserved baseline + burst on demand.
Anna P: Proposal for roadmap/backlog: create a triage ticket: P1 customer intake -> product backlog epic "MapleBank Dedicated sizing + burst SLA". Deliverables: final sizing calc, cost estimate, autoscale policy config, canary runbook, SLA language. Target: 2-week turnaround.
Devon R: Ops/Infra notes: need autoscaler policy draft. Suggest policy skeleton below for initial eval:
```
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 6
  max_replicas: 24
  scale_metric: inflight_requests_per_gpu
  target_value: 8
  cooldown_seconds: 180
  burst_mode: enabled
  burst_multiplier: 3
  burst_duration_sec: 600
```
Devon R: Also add a fallback model variant (smaller quantized) to keep availability if capacity constrained.
Anna P: Sounds good. Kevin, can you confirm customer willingness to accept baseline reservation + burst pricing, and whether they want a hard SLA or best-effort? That will affect priority.
Kevin S: I'll confirm pricing acceptance today. MapleBank prefers a hard SLA for market-open windows but may accept an initial POC with best-effort. I'll update by EOD.
InfraBot: New ticket created: PROD-5421 - "MapleBank dedicated sizing & burst SLA" assigned to @Anna P / @Sarah L / @Devon R, priority P1.
Anna P: Going to add this to next sprint planning + schedule a 30m scoping with customer and infra next Tue. :calendar: :thumbsup:
